rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early-stage neighborhood-living massing: a compact rectilinear volume with a clear central courtyard/slot, an upper bridging condition, and a reasonably legible relationship between solid perimeter and open core. It responds acceptably to the parcel and maintains continuity across all four views, so it is not merely coherent in one projection or a set of colliding solids. The thick blue access edge is answered by a visible ground-level opening/void logic rather than a sealed front, which supports the required public threshold. The main weakness is that the silhouette remains somewhat box-derived and the section is not especially expressive; the form is coherent but not yet strongly profiled or sectionally advanced. Program fit is therefore positive, since neighborhood living can plausibly be supported by this active-edge court composition, but the roof/section logic is still modest compared with the stronger reference set.
